Team — quick read-through and proposed approach below. I pasted suggested redline language at the bottom. High-level: we want to avoid opening general court access for injunctive remedies while being reasonable for a sophisticated customer.

Governing law: Redwood prefers California law (our standard) because it reduces litigation risk and aligns with precedent. If Nexwell insists on Delaware we should evaluate whether the deal economics justify concession; sales should confirm materiality.

Equitable relief / provisional measures: Agree to a narrow carve. Proposed compromise: allow Nexwell to seek provisional injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction where Nexwell has a principal place of business or has obtained emergency relief, but require that (i) such request is limited to preservation of rights and urgent non-monetary relief, and (ii) the claim for substantive relief (monetary damages or declaratory relief) must be stayed for arbitration. This preserves our arbitration preference for merits while acknowledging emergency relief needs. Also require notice to Redwood counsel and 48-hour meet-and-confer if practicable.

Arbitration seat: We normally use California (San Francisco) or AAA/JAMS equivalents. If Nexwell wants JAMS SF and Delaware law, that’s a tricky combo but not impossible. Recommend offering: California law with JAMS (SF). If they insist on Delaware law, we ask for split — Delaware law for contract interpretation, California as procedural seat — but that is messy.

Draft language (for MSA):
"Notwithstanding Section [X], either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve rights pending resolution of the dispute, provided that any substantive claims shall be resolved pursuant to the arbitration provisions of this Agreement and any provisional relief shall be limited to preservation of the status quo and non-monetary relief. The seeking party shall, where practicable, provide notice to the other party and counsel at least 48 hours prior to seeking such relief and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to meet-and-confer prior to filing."

We should also add a service-of-process clause to the order form that permits counsel/service via registered agent in Delaware or CA if needed.

If sales confirms the deal is high priority, we can be flexible on governing law but should capture an explicit concession trade (e.g., additional term commitment or higher rates).

Laura Bennett
General Counsel (acting)
